digest:
## 🔬 Major Technical Developments

### Japan's Successful Mach-5 Ramjet Engine Trial
URL: https://www.bgr.com/2178211/japan-hypersonic-engine-ramjet-2-hour-flights-to-us/
Japan demonstrates working hypersonic propulsion technology for commercial aviation.
This positions Japanese aerospace as a serious contender in the nascent hypersonic travel market. Two-hour transpacific flights would fundamentally reshape business travel economics and real estate valuations in gateway cities. Watch for follow-on defense applications and which Western primes seek licensing deals.

### Norway's 2PB Huawei Flash Deployment for LLM Training
URL: https://www.blocksandfiles.com/flash/2026/05/22/norways-2-petabytes-of-huawei-flash-storage-and-llm-training/5244910
European sovereign AI infrastructure increasingly relies on Chinese hardware despite geopolitical tensions.
Norway's willingness to deploy Huawei at scale for AI workloads signals a pragmatic split from US-aligned tech policy. This creates interesting arbitrage for European AI ventures operating outside US export control constraints. Storage infrastructure is becoming the quiet battleground in AI sovereignty plays.

### Serving Files Three Ways: sync, epoll, io_uring
URL: https://theconsensus.dev/p/2026/05/18/serving-files-three-ways.html
Deep technical comparison of Linux I/O models reveals io_uring's production-readiness trajectory.
io_uring adoption is a leading indicator for infrastructure software performance improvements. Companies still running epoll-based stacks have measurable efficiency gaps. This matters for cloud cost optimization at scale—expect infrastructure vendors to market io_uring support as premium.

## 💼 Business & Market Signals

### ClickUp Mass Layoff: Replacing Hundreds with AI Agents
URL: https://techcrunch.com/2026/05/25/what-clickups-mass-layoff-tells-us-about-the-future-of-work/
Nine-year-old productivity startup substitutes human workforce with AI agents at scale.
This is the first major SaaS company to publicly frame layoffs as direct AI substitution rather than "restructuring." ClickUp's bet signals that AI agent tooling has crossed a capability threshold for internal operations. The playbook will spread—HR tech and workforce planning software face existential product questions.

### eSports Startup Raises $20M by Reframing for AI-Obsessed VCs
URL: https://techcrunch.com/2026/05/25/the-pitch-trick-that-helped-an-esports-startup-raise-20m-when-vcs-only-wanted-ai/
Lucra Sports closes round by positioning against dominant VC thesis rather than conforming to it.
This is useful signal on LP pressure driving AI-or-nothing mandates at growth funds. Founders in non-AI verticals should note the contrarian positioning worked precisely because it acknowledged the market reality. Also suggests eSports betting infrastructure remains underinvested relative to market size.

### Pope Leo XIV's AI Encyclical as Tech Policy Document
URL: https://techcrunch.com/2026/05/25/the-popes-ai-encyclical-isnt-really-about-ai/
Vatican uses AI framing to critique concentrated tech power and democratic erosion.
Magnifica Humanitas matters less as theology than as a signal of institutional alignment against Big Tech. The encyclical will be cited in EU regulatory proceedings and provides moral cover for aggressive antitrust action. Catholic-aligned political movements in Europe and Latin America now have doctrinal backing for tech intervention.

## 📋 Case Studies & Deep Dives

### Using AI to Write Better Code More Slowly
URL: https://nolanlawson.com/2026/05/25/using-ai-to-write-better-code-more-slowly/
Experienced developer argues AI coding tools optimize for speed at the expense of understanding.
This cuts against the dominant "10x productivity" narrative from AI coding tool vendors. The piece suggests a bifurcation: junior developers may become dependent on AI-generated code they don't understand, while senior engineers use AI as review infrastructure. Implications for technical due diligence on software companies—assess AI tool dependency in engineering orgs.

### How Shamir's Secret Sharing Works
URL: https://ente.com/blog/how-shamirs-secret-sharing-works/
Ente explains the cryptographic primitive underlying modern key management and custody solutions.
Shamir's scheme is foundational to crypto custody, enterprise key management, and distributed signing. Understanding this matters for evaluating security claims from fintech and crypto infrastructure companies. The math is surprisingly accessible—useful for technical DD conversations.

### California Exempts Linux from Age-Verification Law
URL: https://www.tomshardware.com/software/linux/california-moves-to-exempt-linux-from-its-upcoming-age-verification-law-after-backlash-over-forcing-operating-systems-to-collect-users-ages-amendment-proposed-by-the-same-lawmaker-who-wrote-the-original-law
State backtracks on requiring OS-level age verification after open-source community backlash.
The original law was technically illiterate—requiring operating systems to collect user ages. The exemption reveals regulatory capture dynamics: consumer tech giants can comply, open-source alternatives would be killed. Watch for similar carve-outs to become standard in tech regulation, advantaging incumbents.

## ⚡ Signal vs. Noise

The ClickUp story is the week's real signal—we've crossed from "AI will replace jobs someday" to "AI is replacing jobs now, at named companies, with specific headcounts." Meanwhile, the Vatican encyclical and Norway's Huawei deployment both point to a fragmenting global tech order where the US doesn't set the rules. The hypersonic engine trial reminds us that hardware breakthroughs still happen outside software, and whoever cracks commercial hypersonic first owns a category.
